When you search for a **Grammarly review 2026**, you’re likely wondering whether the popular writing assistant still delivers enough value to justify its cost. Over the years, Grammarly has evolved from a simple spell‑checker into a full‑featured writing coach that promises to polish everything from emails to academic papers. In this guide, we’ll break down what’s new in 2026, weigh the pros and cons, look at pricing, and help you decide if it’s worth adding to your toolkit.

## What Is Grammarly?

Grammarly is an AI‑powered writing assistant that works across browsers, desktop apps, and mobile keyboards. It scans your text for grammar, spelling, punctuation, style, and tone issues, offering real‑time suggestions. The 2026 version leans harder into generative AI, letting you rewrite sentences, generate outlines, and even brainstorm ideas directly within the editor.

## Key Features

### Grammar & Spelling
The core engine still catches the usual suspects—subject‑verb agreement, misplaced commas, and typo‑ridden words—but now it also flags subtle nuances like inconsistent verb tenses in long documents.

### Style Suggestions
Beyond correctness, Grammarly offers style tweaks aimed at making your writing clearer and more engaging. It highlights passive voice, overused words, and sentence length variations, encouraging a more dynamic rhythm.

### Plagiarism Checker
Premium users get access to a plagiarism detector that scans billions of web pages and academic databases. In 2026, the tool highlights matched sources and provides citation help in APA, MLA, and Chicago formats.

### Tone Detector
Want to sound friendly, formal, or persuasive? The tone analyzer evaluates your word choice and punctuation, giving you a score and suggestions to shift the tone toward your goal.

### AI Writing Aid
A newer addition is the “Write with AI” button. Highlight a paragraph, click the button, and Grammarly will rewrite it for brevity, clarity, or a specific audience. It can also generate bullet points from a block of text or suggest an opening hook for an essay.

## Pros and Cons

### Advantages
- **Accuracy:** The algorithm catches errors many built‑in checkers miss.
- **Versatility:** Works in Google Docs, Microsoft Word, Outlook, Slack, and even social media composers.
- **Learning Curve:** Explanations help users understand why a change is suggested, turning corrections into mini‑lessons.
- **AI Assistance:** The generative features save time on drafting and rewriting.
- **Cross‑Platform Sync:** Your personal dictionary and settings follow you everywhere.

### Drawbacks
- **Cost:** Premium pricing can feel steep for casual users.
- **Over‑Reliance:** Some writers may lean too heavily on suggestions, dulling their unique voice.
- **Occasional False Positives:** Creative or technical jargon sometimes gets flagged incorrectly.
- **Limited Offline Use:** The desktop app needs an internet connection for most AI features.

## Pricing Plans

### Free Tier
The free version covers basic grammar, spelling, and punctuation checks. It’s sufficient for quick emails or social posts but lacks style advice, plagiarism detection, and AI writing aid.

### Premium Options
As of 2026, Premium is priced at $12/month when billed annually ($144/year) or $30/month on a month‑to‑month basis. This unlocks all advanced checks, the plagiarism scanner, tone adjustments, and the AI rewrite tool.

### Business Plans
Teams can opt for Business at $12.50 per user/month (annual). It adds admin controls, centralized billing, and style guide sharing—ideal for companies that want consistent brand voice across documents.

## Who Should Use It?

### Students
If you’re writing essays, research papers, or theses, the plagiarism checker and citation help can save hours and reduce accidental copying concerns.

### Professionals
From executives drafting reports to marketers crafting copy, the tone detector and style suggestions ensure communication hits the right note.
